p1: [low, ominous] Her DNA was found at forty crime scenes, in three countries. [whispers] Nobody ever saw her face.
[low] Germany, nineteen ninety-three. A woman is found dead. [low, ominous] On a cup... a stranger's DNA.
[low] Then the same DNA turned up again. [low, tense] And again.
[low] A heroin syringe. A cookie, left in a burgled caravan. [low, ominous] Murders. Break-ins.
[low, ominous] The papers called her... the woman without a face.
[low] In two thousand seven, a young police officer was shot dead. [low, ominous] The phantom's DNA was there too.
[low, tense] Then her DNA turned up on a dead man's fingerprints. [whispers] But the DNA was a woman's.
[low] So police tested the cotton swabs.
[low] The swabs were never meant for DNA. [low, ominous] A woman who packed them... had touched them.
[low, ominous] There was no killer. [low] For sixteen years, police had been chasing... a factory worker.
[low] And the officer's real killers? [low, ominous] A neo-Nazi terror cell. [whispers] Not found until twenty eleven.
